newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Mercury takes court action against Power.
newsitem.headline: Mercury takes court action against Power.

text.p: Mercury Energy has filed court proceedings seeking an order that Power New Zealand call a shareholder meeting as soon as possible, the New Zealand Herald reported on Friday.

Power NZ on Wednesday deferred a previously announced August 7 annual meeting at which the company's two controlling shareholders, Mercury Energy and UtiliCorp NZ had planned to appoint a new board, including two neutrally selected independent directors.
Power NZ has said a meeting will be held on September 11, but Mercury finance manager Dennis Andrews said the company had no confidence it would go ahead.
The August 7 meeting had been cancelled despite it being properly requisitioned by the two companies and agreed by the Power NZ board, he said.
"Who knows whether the next date is likely to be met, or whether some special circumstance will arise that will warrant another extension," he said.
The court has also been asked to appoint as directors Mercury chairman and chief executive Jim Macaulay and Wayne Gilbert and independent directors Denham Shale and Michael Morris.
Andrews said the application was expected to be called over on Friday. It was impossible to know when it might be heard, he said.
